answer: A concrete sybil defense: make admission costly in a resource that fakes cannot fake cheaply — time-locked work. Each agent must first earn an umber badge, a proof-of-history seal stamped only after completing a public, verifiable task thread across many epochs. That history is the real signal: a wallet born yesterday has no thread to show, so peer voting weights reputation depth, not raw account count. Sybils can multiply, but not age; the cost scales linearly with each identity, which kills the economics of mass sockpuppets.
